knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Section 8.1: after the peak and the oxidation of chloramines, the breakpoint is reached and further chlorine appears as free chlorine.
Section 8.2: trichloramine escapes readily into air and can badly irritate the eyes, and it grows more at low pH.
Section 8.2: phenolics combine with chlorine to yield chlorinated phenols, and the standard discourages phenolic cleaners near pools.

practicalCriteria: On a supplied pool, calculates combined chlorine from free and total readings and states the correct action.
Checks cleaning product labels on a supplied pool deck, identifies a phenolic product, and removes it from the pool zone.
Explains from a supplied reading why a strong chlorine smell does not automatically mean too much free chlorine.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Chlorine and pH test record for the assessed pool
Assessor observation of the label check
stopWorkCriteria: Phenolic product found in the pool zone: remove it from the area and escalate.
Strong chlorine odour with eye irritation: stop, ventilate, leave if symptoms start, escalate.
Chlorine added before breakpoint is confirmed in a plan without checks: stop dosing and escalate.
